analysis:
The PR adds a macOS-27 gate to scripts/install.sh (`require_supported_macos`, called right after `select_provider_identity` at head ~line 592) and updates three docs (installation.md, quickstart.md, and the provider-release.md excerpt). The gate is a UX and eligibility pre-filter. It refuses a new install when the major macOS version parses as numeric and is below 27. An existing CLI at `$BIN_DIR/$CLI_NAME` or a config at `$PROVIDER_CONFIG` bypasses it with a notice. A non-numeric or unknown version returns 0 (fail-open).

Security review:
- The gate does not authorize serving. Serving authorization remains coordinator-side App Attest (A-016, TB-011, T-052), so the installer-side bypasses are not an authorization regression. A user can trivially skip the gate (edit the script, create a config file, spoof MACOS), and a new provider on an old OS still faces coordinator-side policy.
- The check runs before any download, hash verification or commit, so the bundle hash, codesign and atomic-install controls (TB-003/T-013) are unaffected.
- `MACOS` and `MACOS%%.*` are used only in a numeric test after a digit-only case guard, so there is no injection risk.
- The patch excerpt shows no change to the existing `[ -e ... ]` use of variables. I could not see where `MACOS`, `BIN_DIR`, `CLI_NAME`, `PROVIDER_CONFIG` and `PROVIDER_LABEL` are defined, since only the patch is supplied for install.sh. I assume they are set earlier, because `configure_device_verification` already uses the macOS version.
- The docs changes are consistent with the code in the patch. No threat-model assertions such as the receipt or authorization policy are changed.
- Gap: the install.sh embedded copy in the platform (coordinator/api/install.sh) must be re-synced, but that is an external contract outside the supplied evidence.

No concrete regression was identified.
